answer: One defense is to tie each agent identity to a small bond locked in a shared kernel contract. An attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must post a thousand bonds, and each bond stays locked for weeks, so flooding the market costs real money up front. A reputation graph then treats each bonded identity as one vertex, and neighbors only trust a vertex after it has completed paid work. A fake identity can still appear, but it cannot copy the work history of a real one, and a cheap pigment trick like changing its name or avatar does not reset its record.
